sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Logan County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Three offices split the work. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) values every parcel, the Logan County Sheriff collects the current bill, and the Logan County Clerk inherits any bill still unpaid after April 15.

The Sheriff's Office is at 100 North Owen Street in Russellville, open Monday through Friday from 8 am to 4 pm, phone 270-726-2244. Its county page links to the online payment site. The PVA writes from PO Box 307, Russellville, KY 42276 and answers at 270-726-8334. Its own web page says plainly that it neither sets rates nor collects money. The Clerk's Office is at 229 West 3rd Street (270-726-6061) and keeps weekday hours of 8:00 to 4:30.

Rates come from the elected bodies that levy them: the fiscal court, city councils, school boards and districts such as the extension office, library and health department. The clerk keeps the record of those rates, and the bills are printed after the rates are reported.

sections.h2: What is Logan County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Logan County is a farm and factory county on the Tennessee line, with four cities: Russellville, Adairville, Auburn and Lewisburg. The county covers 557 square miles, 552 of them land, on the southwest edge of the Pennyroyal Plateau. It was cut from Lincoln County on September 1, 1792, and a large share of its early wealth came from dark fired tobacco.

Russellville is the seat, with 7,164 residents in 2020. U.S. 68, 79 and 431 meet there, and the nearest limited-access road is the Natcher Parkway (I-165), about 24 miles northeast. Manufacturers make everything from pet food to plastics, and the largest employer, Logan Aluminum, reports more than 1,300 jobs. Two school systems serve buyers: Russellville Independent Schools (R. E. Stevenson Elementary, Russellville Middle and Russellville High) and Logan County Schools (Logan County High School).

The county's 2020 housing count shows 12,461 units, and about 70 percent of the occupied ones are owner-occupied, so most sellers here own a house outright or with a mortgage rather than renting it out.

sections.h2: How is a Logan County property tax bill figured?
sections.html:
The bill is the taxable assessment multiplied by the combined rate of every district that covers the parcel. Kentucky assesses real estate at fair cash value as of January 1, which the state defines as the price it would bring in a voluntary sale, and farm land may be valued at its agricultural use instead.

The Logan PVA describes the tax roll as a working file that changes with assessments and appeals. Assessed value shown there is before exemptions, so a taxable figure needs the exemption subtracted. As a sketch only, a home valued at the county median of $164,900 with the $49,100 homestead exemption would be taxed on $115,800. Ask the County Clerk for the district rates that apply to your address, because they differ between the city of Russellville, the other small cities and rural parcels.

When a property was bought during the previous year, the state allows the deed price to serve as the listed value for the next January 1, provided nothing about the property changed. That makes the price on a recorded deed matter to the next assessment.

sections.h2: When are Logan County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
The Sheriff mails bills around the start of October, and the state schedule then runs in five steps. Pay early and the discount applies; pay late and penalties stack on a fixed calendar.

  • October 1 to November 1: pay the face amount less 2 percent.
  • November 2 to December 31: pay the face amount.
  • January 1 to January 31: a 5 percent penalty applies.
  • February 1 to April 15: a 21 percent penalty applies.
  • After the close of business April 15: the bill moves to the County Clerk.

Questions about a bill that never arrived go to the Sheriff at 270-726-2244. The PVA's page says tax bills are usually mailed by October 1.

Once a bill reaches the clerk it is called a certificate of delinquency and a lien is recorded against the property. Interest runs at 1 percent per month, and a 10 percent clerk fee and a 20 percent county attorney fee are added. The county attorney's first notice goes out by May 15, and delinquent owners can still arrange an installment plan with that office.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Logan County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with a conference at the PVA office, then file with the County Clerk if you still disagree. A raised assessment comes with a notice that states the inspection dates.

  • The tax roll is open for inspection for 13 days starting the first Monday in May, Monday through Saturday.
  • Hold your PVA conference inside that window.
  • File the appeal at the clerk's office by the close of business on the workday after the window ends.
  • The local board of assessment appeals meets 25 to 35 days after the window closes, and the clerk notifies you of the date.

Bring evidence. The board must deny an appeal that arrives with no facts, so photographs, a recent appraisal, insurance policies, construction costs, or listings and sale contracts all help. A paid representative must be an attorney, accountant, certified or licensed appraiser, licensed broker, or another recognized professional, and must carry a written authorization from you. If the board's decision still leaves you unhappy, the letter explains how to go on to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals. Skipping the local board ends that path.

sections.h2: Is there property tax relief for Logan County homeowners?
sections.html:
Yes, the main one is the homestead exemption. Owners who are 65 or older, or who are classified as totally disabled, deduct $49,100 from the assessed value of the home they live in for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. Proof of age can be a birth certificate, driver's license or passport.

Applications go to the Logan PVA, whose published instructions say to mail them to PO Box 307, Russellville, KY 42276. Disability applicants generally renew every year, unless the disability is a veteran's service-connected one or has been ruled total and permanent by the Social Security Administration or the Kentucky Retirement Systems. The PVA's page also lists exemptions for some religious, educational and governmental property.

Farm owners should ask the PVA about agricultural valuation, since Logan County has a long farming tradition and the state permits farm land to be valued by use.

sections.h2: What happens at the Logan County tax sale?
sections.html:
The clerk lists unpaid bills and, if they are still open, sells them to outside buyers. For the 2025 bills, the Logan County Clerk's page set the sale for Wednesday, July 29, 2026, at 10:00 am in the old courthouse courtroom. Half-page newspaper notices ran June 18 and the full list followed June 29.

Outside buyers register in advance. The clerk's page lists a fee of $5 per prior-year bill and $10 per current-year bill with a $250 cap, a 25 percent deposit on current-year bills and full payment on prior-year bills. A buyer who wins a bill takes over the lien, and the owner then deals with that buyer, who may add substantial fees. State rules require the county attorney to mail a 30-day notice and, if needed, another within 60 days, and the sale must fall between 90 and 135 days after the bills reach the clerk.

Call the clerk well before a sale date if a bill on your house is on the list. Paying the clerk before the sale keeps the lien out of a stranger's hands.

sections.h2: How should I handle property tax when selling a Logan County house?
sections.html:
Ask the Sheriff for the amount due before you sign a contract, and ask the closing agent to show the tax on the settlement statement.

  • Current-year bills are collected by the Sheriff, so a payoff figure for the year comes from the Sheriff's Office at 270-726-2244.
  • Bills from earlier years sit with the County Clerk, with interest and fees added each month.
  • Ask the closing agent to show the tax payoff as a line on the settlement statement so the bill is cleared at the table.
  • If the house is vacant or inherited, confirm who owns it on the tax roll before the sale.

Many Logan County sellers are heirs, landlords or owners of older farmhouses. The sooner you learn the exact balance, the sooner you can work out your net from the sale.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to in Logan County?
faqs.a: Pay the Logan County Sheriff at 100 North Owen Street in Russellville, or through the link on the county's sheriff page. The office is open weekdays from 8 am to 4 pm and answers at 270-726-2244. After April 15 the bill moves to the County Clerk at 229 West 3rd Street.

faqs.q: What discount do I get for paying a Logan County tax bill early?
faqs.a: You get 2 percent off if you pay between October 1 and November 1. From November 2 through December 31 you pay the face amount. A 5 percent penalty starts January 1 and a 21 percent penalty starts February 1.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my Logan County assessment after the inspection period?
faqs.a: No. The appeal must follow a PVA conference and be filed at the clerk's office by the workday after the 13-day inspection window closes. That window opens on the first Monday in May each year, so the next chance comes the following spring.

faqs.q: Does the PVA collect or set my Logan County property tax?
faqs.a: No. The PVA appraises property and handles exemptions, but its own page states that it does not set rates and does not collect payments. Rates come from local taxing bodies and the Sheriff collects.

faqs.q: What if my Logan County property tax bill is delinquent?
faqs.a: Contact the County Clerk's Office at 270-726-6061 for a payoff amount. The bill carries a lien, 1 percent monthly interest and added fees, and it can be offered at the annual tax sale if it stays unpaid. Paying before the sale avoids a third-party buyer.
